chunks: And from him (Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub) from Hammad ibn Isa, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the preparation for Ihram, so he said: 'Trimming the nails, removing the hair of the mustache, and shaving the pubic area.'
ai.seo_question: What are the required grooming acts before entering Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies the *Sunnah* acts of grooming (tahayyu') that a pilgrim must perform before donning the Ihram garments, emphasizing physical purity as a precursor to spiritual consecration. These acts—trimming nails, removing the mustache, and shaving pubic hair—mirror the natural disposition (fitrah) and are considered part of the ritual preparation that distinguishes the pilgrim’s state of sanctity. The emphasis on these specific bodily cleansings underscores the holistic nature of Islamic ritual, where external cleanliness facilitates internal devotion.
